chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ wrote to al-Riḍā عليه السلام:
The people have differed regarding al-rabīthā, so what do you command me concerning it?
So he عليه السلام wrote: “There is no harm in it.”

key_terms.اخْتَلَفَ: differed; indicating the existence of disagreement among people
key_terms.الرَّبِيثَا: al-rabīthā; the disputed subject asked about in the report
key_terms.النَّاسُ: the people; the broader public or community discussing the issue
key_terms.تَأْمُرُنِي: you command me; asking for authoritative guidance
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; a formula indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: What was Imam al-Riḍā’s عليه السلام ruling regarding al-rabīthā?
ai.summary: This hadith records a written legal inquiry to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a disputed matter concerning al-rabīthā. The Imam’s written reply gives a concise ruling of permissibility, stating that there is no harm in it.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4204 - Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' wrote to Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as), saying:
"The people have differed regarding the rabbit (al-rabitha). What do you command me concerning it?"
Imam (as) wrote back: "There is no harm in it."
